testing_note: Dry-ran the skill by hand on a scratch claim (scratch/example.md): six line items including an under-threshold taxi with no receipt, a dinner with wine, a hotel over cap with a mismatched receipt date, an uncovered coworking pass and a possible duplicate dinner with no receipt. The run showed the Approve definition wrongly required a receipt even when the policy waives one, so I added the waiver; and that held items lose the information that a cap will still apply, so open items now note any pending cap or exclusion in their evidence. The reconcile check (approved + reductions + rejected + held = claimed) balanced on the example.
applied_note: I made the skill model-invoked with a short description front-loaded on the leading phrase 'Expense claim review' and a single trigger branch, and kept everything in one SKILL.md because every run needs the verdict definitions, steps and output template, so nothing qualified for disclosure. Each step ends on a checkable, exhaustive completion criterion (every item paired, every item with verdict and evidence, figures that reconcile exactly, a question for every open item), and leading words (evidence, open, reconcile) carry the core behaviours. The 'only the supplied policy' and 'no guessing' requirements are phrased positively (the policy is the whole rulebook; when two verdicts remain plausible the verdict is open) rather than as prohibitions.
model: claude-opus-5-5 (inherited by a fresh general-purpose subagent)
